BREAKING: US oil prices have recorded 3 drawdowns of at least 20% so far in 2026, matching their 2nd-longest such streak since the 1980s.

2020 was the only year with a longer streak, at 4 such declines, while 1990, 1991, 1998, and 2022 each recorded 3.

Taking intraday prices into account, US oil prices have posted 4 drawdowns of at least 20% this year.

Furthermore, oil prices have seen 8 corrections of 10%+ so far in 2026, their longest such streak since 1986.

The same number of 10%+ drawdowns was posted in 1990, 2004, and 2009.

Year-to-date, oil prices are up +42%, on track for the largest annual gain since 2021.

US oil prices have rarely been this volatile.

Brian Chesky used to ask Airbnb candidates if they'd take the job with a year left to live:

"I interviewed the first 300 employees at Airbnb, which people think I'm really neurotic, and that may also be true... I used to ask them, 'If you had a year left to live, would you take this job?' And actually the people who say yes to that you probably don't want because they should probably spend time with [their] family. So I amended it to 10 years."

"I really wanted people to think about that. That was enough time for you to do something you really cared about. And the answer doesn't have to be this company. And I say, 'Fine, if what you're meant to do is to travel... you should just do that. Don't come here. Go do that.'"

"Two men are laying bricks. Somebody comes up to the first man and says, 'What are you doing?' He says, 'I'm building a wall.' He asks the other guy, 'What are you doing?' He says, 'I'm building a cathedral.'"

"There is a job, and then there's a calling. And we want to hire people that aren't just looking for jobs. They're looking for a calling. And that's kind of the first value, and that's champion the mission."

@bchesky at Stanford, 2014

Gold has rarely been this oversold:

Gold prices are trading -20% below their 200-day moving average, their largest negative deviation since June 2013.

This marks a sharp reversal from the +45% deviation above the 200-day moving average recorded in January, the largest since the 1970s.

This comes as gold prices have dropped -37% from their January intraday peak, their largest drawdown within a 12-month period since the early 1980s.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, gold prices also declined -20% below their 200-day moving average.

However, the largest such negative deviation was recorded in 1981, at -27%.

Gold is experiencing one of its most severe declines in history.

For those of us left here in crypto, as we wallow in sorrow, there are some interesting analogies to consider about where we are right now and what we're seeing in DeFi from a revenue-generation perspective, not to mention the improving value accrual trend: it is akin to the Nasdaq post the 2001 bubble burst.

If 2021 marked the hype-cycle peak for crypto, which it most certainly was, driven by excess liquidity and a pre-AI world, then DeFi is doing exactly what the Nasdaq did in the years that followed. Adoption is accelerating, revenues are expanding, and multiples are compressing. 

By 2006, the NDX had 2-3x from the lows and its P/E halved. 

In DeFi, revenue is 5.5x, and the multiple is sub-10x (down 80%). At some point, this matters. 

... unless, of course, 2027/2028 turns into a 2007/2008! Not my base case!
